results.title: TSMC looks to accelerate advanced process expansion
results.description:
# TSMC accelerates advanced process expansion as 3nm and 2nm capacity ramps
TSMC looks to expand 3nm and 2nm capacity Credit: adobe.stock.com

The reported increase would place TSMC ahead of previous market expectations and further strengthen its position in the race to supply advanced chips for artificial intelligence, high-performance computing and data centre applications.

Alongside its 3nm ramp-up, TSMC’s 2nm programme is also said to be progressing on schedule, with monthly wafer starts expected to approach 100,000 units by the end of 2026.

Combined output from the company’s 2nm and 3nm process technologies could exceed 260,000 wafers per month by early fourth quarter, providing additional momentum for revenue growth.

The company has announced additional 3nm production facilities in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan, while also repurposing existing 5nm manufacturing equipment in Taiwan to increase 3nm output.

The foundry is also preparing for a major expansion of its 2nm capacity. The company has stated that first-year output from its 2nm process is expected to be 45% higher than the initial production volume achieved by its 3nm technology in 2023.

As demand for AI processors and next-generation computing platforms continues to grow, TSMC’s aggressive expansion highlights the growing importance of manufacturing capacity in the global semiconductor industry.

## Semiconductor Equipment Faces Supply Shortages as Well ... ASML Says Next Year's Orders Are Already Secured
(ASML), which makes extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment for advanced semiconductor manufacturing, raised its full-year revenue outlook by more than 5 billion euros, or about 8 trillion won, from 36 billion to 40 billion euros announced in its first-quarter earnings release to 43 billion to 45 billion euros in last month's second-quarter results. The revision appears to reflect a sharp increase in orders from major customers including Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, TSMC and Intel.

Other top global semiconductor equipment makers, including Applied Materials, Inc., Lam Research and Tokyo Electron, are also expected to see a sharp rise in orders. According to the Bank of Korea, imports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment in the first half of this year totaled $18.76 billion, up 38.8% from a year earlier. Imports from foreign semiconductor equipment companies are surging.
